DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov_ph DILG OPINION No. 47 s. 2022 June 3, 2022 HON. DIEGO "NONOY" TY Representative ISt District, Misamis Occidental Misamis Occidental ISt District Congressional Office Mabini Street, Southem Poblacion Paridel, Misamis Occidental Dear Honorable Ty: This refers to your letter bringing to the Departments attention the plight of the Local Government Unit of Plaridel, concerning the decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental on an administrative case filed by Job Order Employees. Based on the documents forwarded to the DILG-CentraI Office, the factual antecedents of the present controversy are as follows: I. The Sanggunian Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental, in a decision on an administrative case, found Mayor Alicia Rama-Ty, Vice-Mayor Rolando Manuel C- Ty and Sangguniang Bayan Member Jude! R Ty, liable for abuse of authority and grave misconduct and were meted with the penalty of six-month suspension. 2. The respondents voluntarily commenced the service of said penalty despite the absence of an implementing order from the Govemor, and was followed by the turn-over of office facilitated by DILG Officer, MLGOO VI Harold Buscaino. 3. As reported, Land Bank of the Philippines denied the processing of the newly assumed Mayor Prince Kien Bandiala's authority for the LGU's financial transactions in view of the absence of the Govemor's order implementing the suspension order of the Sanggunian Panlalawigan's decision. It is for this reason that you are seeking legal advice and guidance from the Department as to what proper steps to be undertaken to resolve the present predicament faced by the Municipality of Plaridel. In this regard, may we invite your attention to Sections 61, 66, 67 and 68 of RA 7160 of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 , which provide: "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No-: 8876-W54

"SECTION 61. Form and Filing of Administrative Complaints. — A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: (b) A complaint against any elective official of a municipality shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; xxx "SECTION 66. Form and Notice of Decision. - (a) The investigation of the case shall be terminated within ninety (90) days from the start thereof. Within thirty (30) days afier the end of the investigation, the Office of the President or the Sanggunian concerned shall render a decision in writing stating clearly and distinctly the facts and the reasons for such decision. Copies of said decision shall immediately be fumished the respondent and all interested parties. (b) The penalty of suspension shall not exceed the unexpired term of the respondent or a period of six (6) months for every administrative offense, nor shall said penalty be a bar to the candidacy of the respondent so suspended as long as he meets the qualifications required for the office. (c) The penalty of removal from office as a result of an administrative investigation shall be considered a bar to the candidacy of the respondent for any elective position." "SECTION 67. Administrative Appeals. - Decisions in administrative cases may, within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof, be appealed to the following: (a) The Sangguniang Panlalawigan, in the case of decisions of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of component cities and the Sangguniang bayan; and (b) The Office of the President, in the case of decisions of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and the Sangguniang Panlungsod of highly urbanized cities and independent component cities. Decisions of the Office of the President shall be final and executory." "SECTION 68. Execution Pending Appeal. - An appeal shall not prevent a decision from becoming final or executory. The respondent shall be considered as having been placed under preventive suspension during the pendency of an appeal in the event he wins such appeal. In the event the appeal results in an exoneration, he shall be paid his salary and such other emoluments during the pendency of the appeal." Based on the foregoing, a verified complaint against any erring any elective official of a municipality shall be filed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, After the Sangguniang Panlalawigan decided the administrative case within the time specified in the aforequoted provisions, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan may direct the Governor to implement its decision. If the Governor is being directed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to implement its decision or judgment rendered pursuant to the exercise of its quasi-judicial powers conferred by Section 61 of the Code, it is the ministerial duty of the Govemor to execute the same and he/she has no discretion to determine the propriety of the implementation of the decision or judgment.

The service or implementation of the decision/judgment has to be made without unnecessary delay so that after being duly informed, the respondent can immediately take steps to protect his interest by filing an appeal or apply for other appropriate relief. In this regard, please be informed that in a Memorandum from the Executive Secretary dated 01 December 2021 re: APPELLA TE JURISDICTIOM OF THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT OVER SUSPENSION ORDERS AGAINST LOCAL ELECTIVE OFFICIALS, the Department was advised, among others, that the Office of the President "xxx has authority to order the stay of execution of the final decisions or orders of suspension from omce issued by the Sanggunians against local elective officials, pursuant to Section 9 of AO No. 22 and consistent with the Supreme Court ruling in Berces Sr. v. Executive Secretary. " However, as you have represented, notwithstanding the failure of the Governor to issue an order implementing the 07 January 2022 Decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental against the respondents, namely: Mayor Alicia Rama-Ty, Vice-Mayor Rolando Manuel C. Ty and the Sangguniang Bayan Member Judel R. Ty, respondents undertook to heed to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Decision, voluntarily vacated their posts and tumed them over to the next-in-rank Sangguniang Bayan Members. Now, the issue boils down to whether or not the respondents can voluntarily vacate their posts and tum them over to the next-in-rank Sangguniang Bayan Members even without the implementation order from the Governor. We reply in the affirmative. The first sentence of Section 68 of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 states that an appeal shall not prevent a decision from becoming final or executory. This therefore emphasizes the executory nature of the Decision of the Sanggunian pursuant to its quasi-judicial function. We also mentioned in our discussion above that if the Governor is being directed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan to implement its decision or judgment, it is a ministerial duty on his part to implement the same. In the instant case, the reason for the failure of the Governor to issue an order implementing the January 7, 2022 Decision of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Misamis Occidental against the respondents was not stated in your letter. Accordingly, notwithstanding the absence of an order from the Governor implementing the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Decision, we are of the view that respondents can voluntarily vacate their respective posts and serve their suspension order. The implementation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan cannot be made subservient to the actions of the Govemor. At this juncture, may it be respectfully informed that incidents of voluntary service of suspension are no longer new to the Department. There were several local elective officials had also previously undertook to voluntary serve their suspension involving cases filed before the Sandiganbayan. The Department sees no reason why said voluntary service could not be applied in administrative cases. However, said willingness of the respondents to voluntarily serve their suspension to comply with the orders of Sangguniang Panlalawigan must be manifested first in writing to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Respectfully yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARLO L. Undersecr I GAN ry for Local Govemment OUSLG/MLl/LLLS/LRALLD'kbrn/c1p/ML1 cc: DIR. ARNEL M.
